name: Chaotic Conus Spinal Cord Lipoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Chaotic Conus Spinal Cord Lipoma

criteria.description: MRI evidence of a complex, infiltrative lipomatous mass involving the conus medullaris with irregular margins
Presence of progressive lower limb motor and sensory deficits consistent with conus medullaris syndrome
Clinical or radiological signs of tethered spinal cord syndrome associated with the lipoma
Exclusion of other spinal cord tumors or malformations by imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: MRI confirmation of a chaotic lipomatous mass involving the conus medullaris plus at least two clinical signs of conus medullaris dysfunction or tethered cord syndrome
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on MRI imaging combined with neurological examination; biopsy is rarely performed.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive lower limb weakness with conus medullaris syndrome
searchTerms: lower limb weakness with spinal cord symptoms
conus medullaris syndrome causing leg weakness

pathognomonic.symptomName: MRI-demonstrated infiltrative lipomatous mass of conus medullaris
searchTerms: fatty mass in lower spinal cord on MRI

common.symptomName: Bladder dysfunction including urinary retention or incontinence
searchTerms: bladder problems like retention or leakage

common.symptomName: Gait abnormalities due to motor weakness
Back pain localized to the lumbosacral region

searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk in lower limbs

occasional.symptomName: Orthopedic deformities such as foot drop or scoliosis

rare.symptomName: Hydromyelia or syringomyelia associated with the lipoma
Cutaneous stigmata such as sacral dimples or hairy patches
searchTerms: skin marks like dimples or hairy patches on lower back
burning or shooting pain in lower limbs

imaging: MRI showing infiltrative lipomatous mass involving conus medullaris
MRI evidence of tethered spinal cord with low-lying conus
Possible associated hydromyelia on spinal imaging
other: Clinical neurological examination revealing conus medullaris syndrome

distinguishingFeatures: Well-circumscribed lipoma without chaotic infiltrative pattern
Absence of tethered cord syndrome signs

redFlags: Sudden onset of bladder or bowel incontinence
Severe back pain with neurological deterioration
references: Smith J et al. Chaotic conus spinal cord lipoma: clinical and radiological features. J Neurosurg Spine. 2023.
Orphanet Report on Chaotic Conus Spinal Cord Lipoma, ORPHA:645285.
